# Metrics as Baseline deviation (for cor, GEER, validation of GEER:
## 1. Metrics as Baseline deviation: ΔGEER 

### Why deviation metric: 
 - Absolute GEER values are not directly comparable across harvests because each harvest has a different baseline level of predictability. 
 - Expressing model performance as deviation from the baseline (ΔG) removes this baseline effect and isolates the marginal contribution of the spatial model.  
 - This allows results from multiple harvests to be combined and compared on a common scale.

### What is deviaiton? 
Baseline = Base model (no spatial correction)
Models = Spa (AR1), PEE (RR)

So for each replicate-pair GEER:
 1. ΔG_Spa = GEER_Spa − GEER_Base
 2. ΔG_PEE = GEER_PEE − GEER_Base

### What it tells?
 - how much does each model improve over baseline?
 - Isolates gain from spatial correction like AR or RR(PEE). 


All harvests (in each rep, we do the subtraction)

##### 1. Deviation GEER
```{r All harvests, deviation GEER, et22, 04212026}
## ============================================================
## ALL HARVESTS: ΔGEER (relative to baseline)
## et22
## ============================================================

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## Step 1: Convert combined GEER results to wide format
## ------------------------------------------------------------
GEER_delta_et22 <- GEER_all_et22 %>%
  dplyr::select(Harvest, Rep1, Rep2, Model, Pearson) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Model, values_from = Pearson)
GEER_delta_et22

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## Step 2: Compute ΔGEER for each model
## ------------------------------------------------------------
GEER_delta_et22 <- GEER_delta_et22 %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    AR = `Spa(AR)` - Base,
    RR = PEE - Base)


## ------------------------------------------------------------
## Step 3: Convert to long format
## ------------------------------------------------------------
GEER_delta_et22 <- GEER_delta_et22 %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(AR, RR),
    names_to = "Model",
    values_to = "Delta")


## ------------------------------------------------------------
## Step 4: Ensure consistent ordering
## ------------------------------------------------------------
GEER_delta_et22$Model <- factor(
  GEER_delta_et22$Model,
  levels = c("AR", "RR"))
GEER_delta_et22

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## Step 5: Plot ΔGEER across all harvests
## ------------------------------------------------------------
ggplot(GEER_delta_et22, aes(x = Model, y = Delta, fill = Model)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.15, outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.3) +
  # geom_jitter(width = 0.08, size = 2) +
  stat_summary(
    fun = mean,
    geom = "point",
    shape = 18,
    size = 3,
    color = "red") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(-0.1, 1, by = 0.1)) +
  ylab(expression(Delta~GEER)) +
  ggtitle("ET22 All Harvests: GEER Improvement over Baseline (ΔGEER)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

```{rΔCOR et22, 04212026}
## ΔCOR: Fit vs Observed correlation (relative to Base)

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## Step 1: Create table manually (per yield)
## ------------------------------------------------------------

cor_et22 <- data.frame(
  Harvest = paste0("YLD", c(1,2,3,5)),
  Base = c(
    cor_fit_obs_base_yld1_et22,
    cor_fit_obs_base_yld2_et22,
    cor_fit_obs_base_yld3_et22, # removed yld4 from here compared to NOR
    cor_fit_obs_base_yld5_et22), # only upto yld5
  AR = c(
    cor_fit_obs_spa_yld1_et22,
    cor_fit_obs_spa_yld2_et22,
    cor_fit_obs_spa_yld3_et22,
    cor_fit_obs_spa_yld5_et22),
  RR = c(
    cor_fit_obs_pee_yld1_et22,
    cor_fit_obs_pee_yld2_et22,
    cor_fit_obs_pee_yld3_et22,
    cor_fit_obs_pee_yld5_et22))

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## Step 2: Compute ΔCOR
## ------------------------------------------------------------
cor_delta_et22 <- cor_et22 %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    AR = AR - Base, # here AR-base
    RR = RR - Base) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(AR, RR),
    names_to = "Model",
    values_to = "Delta")

  geom_boxplot(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.05, size = 2) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", shape = 18, size = 3, color = "red") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  ylab(expression(Delta~COR)) +
  ggtitle("ET22: All Harvests- Fitted vs Observed Yields (ΔCOR)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

```{r VAL: Validation of GEER (AR, RR vs Base GBLUP), et22, 06072026 }
  Base = c(0.63,	0.84,	0.80,	0.82), # from above chunks saved in excel and grabbed from there

  RR = c(0.96, 0.95, 0.96, 0.95))

## YLD3
val_yld3_et22 <- data.frame(
  Harvest = "YLD3", Rep = 1:4,
  Base = c(0.71,	0.87,	0.88,	0.85), # from above chunks saved in excel and grabbed from there
  AR = c(0.66, 0.83, 0.81, 0.91),
  RR = c(0.89, 0.89, 0.88, 0.85))

## YLD5
val_yld5_et22 <- data.frame(
  Harvest = "YLD5", Rep = 1:4,
  Base = c(0.60,	0.86,	0.85,	0.85), # from above chunks saved in excel and grabbed from there
  AR = c(0.64, 0.86, 0.83, 0.85),
  RR = c(0.71, 0.86, 0.83, 0.84))

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## Step 2: Combine
## ------------------------------------------------------------
val_all_et22 <- rbind(
  val_yld1_et22,
  val_yld2_et22,
  val_yld3_et22,
  val_yld5_et22)

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## Step 3: Long format
## ------------------------------------------------------------
val_long_et22 <- val_all_et22 %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Base, AR, RR),
    names_to = "Model",
    values_to = "Value")

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## Step 4: Ensure consistent ordering
## ------------------------------------------------------------
val_long_et22$Model <- factor(
  val_long_et22$Model,
  levels = c("Base", "AR", "RR"))
# export this file
write.csv(val_long_et22, file = "2022/MSI_data/output_files/valGEER_ET22_NMSU.csv", col.names = TRUE)


## ------------------------------------------------------------
## Step 5: Plot
## ------------------------------------------------------------
## ------------------------------------------------------------
## Step 5: Plot validation correlations
## ------------------------------------------------------------

gg_val_long_et22 <- ggplot(val_long_et22, aes(x = Model, y = Value,fill = Model)) + # !!
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.3, alpha = 0.9,outlier.shape = NA) +
  labs(
    title = "ET2022 All Harvests: Validation GEER with base GBLUP", # !!
    x = "Model",
    y = "Validation GEER (correlation)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 13) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Base" = "gray",
      "AR" = "lightblue",
      "RR" = "lightgreen")) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1),
    breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.2)) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "right")
gg_val_long_et22

ggsave(filename = "ValGEER_boxplots_ET_2022_NMSU.png", plot = gg_val_long_et22, path = "2022/output_images", width = 10, height = 10,dpi = 400)


```

```{r Combine all GEER deviations from 4 trials of NMSU, 06172026}
# Read files
GEER_delta_nor22 <- read.csv("2022/MSI_data/output_files/GEER_original&deviations_Nor22_NMSU.csv") %>%
  select(-X)

GEER_delta_et22 <- read.csv("2022/MSI_data/output_files/GEER_original&deviations_ET22_NMSU.csv") %>%
  select(-X)

GEER_delta_nor23 <- read.csv("2023/MSI_data/output_files/GEER_original&deviations_Nor23_NMSU.csv") %>%
  select(-X)

GEER_delta_et23 <- read.csv("2023/MSI_data/output_files/GEER_original&deviations_ET23_NMSU.csv") %>%
  select(-X)

# Add trial labels
GEER_delta_nor22$Trial <- "NOR22"
GEER_delta_et22$Trial  <- "ET22"
GEER_delta_nor23$Trial <- "NOR23"
GEER_delta_et23$Trial  <- "ET23"

# Combine
geer_all_nmsu <- bind_rows(GEER_delta_nor22, GEER_delta_et22, GEER_delta_nor23, GEER_delta_et23)

# Clean labels
geer_all_nmsu$Model <- factor(
  geer_all_nmsu$Model,
  levels = c("AR","RR"))

geer_all_nmsu$Trial <- factor(
  geer_all_nmsu$Trial,
  levels = c("NOR22","ET22","NOR23","ET23"))

# Create pair labels
geer_all_nmsu$TrialModel <- paste(geer_all_nmsu$Model,
                             geer_all_nmsu$Trial,
                             sep = "-")
geer_all_nmsu
# Plot



#try boxplots grouped

gg_GEER_deviation_all_nmsu <- ggplot(geer_all_nmsu,aes(x=Trial,y=Delta,fill=Model)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.5, alpha = 0.9,outlier.shape = NA) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "AR" = "lightblue",
    "RR"     = "lightgreen")) +
  labs(
    title = "GEER Deviation from Base Model in NMSU Trials",
    x = "trials",
    y = expression(Delta * "GEER")) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 17) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 0.8),
    breaks = seq(0, 0.8, by = 0.2))  +
  theme(
  plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = 20),
  axis.text = element_text(size = 18, color = "black"),
  axis.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold"),
  legend.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold"),
  legend.text = element_text(size = 16),
  legend.position = "right"
)
gg_GEER_deviation_all_nmsu

ggsave(filename = "Combined_GEER_deviation_boxplots_All_Trials_NMSU.png", plot = gg_GEER_deviation_all_nmsu, path = "2022/output_images", width = 10, height = 10,dpi = 400)
```
